results.label: this tree ships the M110 news-window module (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the rule is a leaf module: it requires nothing at all, so it cannot pull in the app, a database or a test helper
and it reads no environment, no filesystem, no absolute path and not even the clock: `now` is passed in, so its decision is reproducible from its arguments alone
every shipped importer reaches it by a relative path inside the tree, so a copy of the tree needs nothing outside it
no shipped file mentions this milestone’s harness, its shim or its probes: the tests measure the product, the product does not know about the tests
copied out of the repository, the module produces byte-identical decisions — the rule is the file, not the checkout
a backup carries the pair out, so a trader can see which window their own archive was taken under — as two columns, with no single knob beside them
a foreign bundle imports (so the next result is a real import, not a refused request)
and it CANNOT move the importing desk’s pair: a looser 1/240 in an archive does not become this trader’s window
it also does not create an account from the bundle: an archive restores trades, never desks or their settings
the imported trade was mapped onto the named desk, which is what makes the untouched pair a result rather than a no-op
a bundle from the previous release (accounts with no news keys at all) imports without inventing one
keys declared at the ROOT of a bundle are ignored rather than applied: the import surface has no news authority
and the pair is nowhere in the bundle’s own vocabulary: no import code path writes the news columns
a CSV import carries no settings of any kind and leaves the pair alone
a desk with no stored pair is reported as `default` on both sides, so an unanswered setting is visible instead of passing as a stored one
research overrides are per request and never written back: after a widened research call the stored pair is still the trader’s own

scope: M110 portability: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock and a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser; two asymmetric news clocks, no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
